title: Descent of a base-change-compatible source-open locus through an equivalence relation
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. For each flat [def-weil-flat-morphism] locally finitely presented [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation] morphism $f:X\to Y$ of $S$-schemes, suppose an open subscheme $D_f\subseteq X$ [def-weil-open-immersion] is assigned. Assume this assignment is invariant under isomorphisms of morphisms, and for every cartesian square [def-pc-fibre-product] with $f:X\to Y$, $g:Y'\to Y$, $f':X\times_YY'\to Y'$ all flat and locally of finite presentation, the equality $D_{f'}=\operatorname{pr}_X^{-1}(D_f)$ holds. Let $V,R$ be $S$-schemes and $(s,t):R\to V\times_SV$ a scheme equivalence relation: for every $S$-scheme $T$, this map injects $R(T)$ into $V(T)\times V(T)$ as an equivalence relation. Suppose $s,t$ are flat and locally of finite presentation. Let $e:V\to R$ be the unique morphism with $s e=t e=\mathrm{id}_V$, supplied by reflexivity on sections. Then the open subscheme $W=e^{-1}(D_s)$ satisfies $D_s=t^{-1}(W)$ as open subschemes of $R$.

source.place: Tag 04LH, label lemma-local-source, case g=id and Q=R=flat and locally of finite presentation; the proof identifies W as the inverse image along the identity section.

proof.text: For every $S$-scheme $T$, reflexivity, symmetry and transitivity give the identity, inverse and composition on the relation $R(T)\subseteq V(T)^2$. Each operation is natural in $T$: its endpoints are natural, and the injectivity of $R(T)\to V(T)^2$ forces uniqueness. The Yoneda bijection therefore gives scheme morphisms $e,i,c$, with $c(a,b)=a\circ b$ for $s(a)=t(b)$. The groupoid laws hold because both sides have the same endpoints on every test scheme. This equips $R\rightrightarrows V$ with the groupoid structure of [def-a1-groupoid-scheme], and its identity is the specified $e$.

source.place: Tag 0233, lemma-equivalence-groupoid; Yoneda construction of the unique operations.

proof.text: Put $A=R\times_{t,V,t}R$ with projections $p_0,p_1$, and let $d(a,b)=i(a)\circ b$. The translation isomorphism [lem-a1-groupoid-source-pullback-translation], together with inversion and interchange of factors, gives isomorphisms $A\to B=R\times_{t,V,s}R$, $(a,b)\mapsto(d(a,b),a)$, and $A\to C=R\times_{s,V,s}R$, $(a,b)\mapsto(d(a,b),b)$. Their inverses are respectively $(z,a)\mapsto(a,a\circ z)$ and $(z,b)\mapsto(b\circ i(z),b)$; the inverse identities are precisely associativity, inverse and unit laws. To see the first directly from that cited translation, apply its inverse to $(i(b),i(a))$ and invert both output arrows. For the second apply its inverse to $(i(a),i(b))$ and invert the second output arrow. Consequently the squares with top $d:A\to R$, bottom $s:R\to V$, and vertical pairs $(p_0,t)$ and $(p_1,s)$ are cartesian: $t d=s p_0$ and $s d=s p_1$.

source.place: Tag 04LH, lemma-local-source, proof with g=id; cartesian division diagram from groupoids.tex Tag 03C6 (lemma-diagram-pull).

proof.text: The two squares identify $d$ as the base change of $s$ along $s$ and along $t$, respectively. Thus $d$ is flat by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-base-change] and locally of finite presentation by clause (3) of [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence]. All morphisms required in the assignment hypothesis are therefore flat and locally of finite presentation: the original $s$, each base morphism $s$ or $t$, and the base-changed $d$. Base-change compatibility and invariance under the two displayed isomorphisms give $D_d=p_0^{-1}(D_s)$ and $D_d=p_1^{-1}(D_s)$, hence $p_0^{-1}(D_s)=p_1^{-1}(D_s)$ as open subschemes of $A$.

source.place: Tag 04LH, lemma-local-source, proof with g=id; cartesian division diagram from groupoids.tex Tag 03C6 (lemma-diagram-pull).

proof.text: The identity $t e=\mathrm{id}_V$ gives a morphism $j:R\to A$, $r\mapsto(r,e(t(r)))$, by the fibre-product universal property. Its composites are $p_0j=\mathrm{id}_R$ and $p_1j=e t$. Taking inverse images of the equality in the preceding step along $j$ yields $D_s=(e t)^{-1}(D_s)=t^{-1}(e^{-1}(D_s))=t^{-1}(W)$. The inverse image $W=e^{-1}(D_s)$ is open because $e$ is continuous; the open-immersion definition identifies an open subscheme with the restricted structure sheaf on its open subset, so these inverse-image identities are identities of open subschemes.

The item's statement and stmt_deps match clones/live exactly, where the item is still unsplit with no repair note. The hypotheses match 04LH with g=id and Q=R=flat+lfp. The explicit invariance-under-isomorphisms assumption stands in for the intrinsic W(P,f). This is what the citer lem-sfb-flat-relation-cm-open uses. Step 1 builds e, i and c by Yoneda from injectivity on T-points; marking it elementary is fine. Step 2: the cited translation is F(a,b)=(a∘b,b) with inverse G(d,b)=(d∘i b,b). I checked by hand that G(i b,i a) with both factors inverted gives (d,a) in R×_{t,s}R, and G(i a,i b) with the second factor inverted gives (d,b) in R×_{s,s}R. Both inverses check, and t d = s p0, s d = s p1. Step 3: square B has f=s, g=t, pr_X=p0; square C has f=s, g=s, pr_X=p1. All three morphisms are flat and lfp by the base-change leaves, so D_d=p0^{-1}D_s=p1^{-1}D_s. The section e is never fed into the assignment. Step 4 pulls back along j=(id,e t), giving D_s=t^{-1}e^{-1}D_s. Edge cases (empty, diagonal, indiscrete) are consistent. lean.statement: theorem relation_open_locus_descent {S : Scheme.{u}} (D : ∀ {X Y : Over S} (f : X ⟶ Y), Flat f.left → LocallyOfFinitePresentation f.left → X.left.Opens) (hiso : ∀ {X Y X' Y' : Over S} (f : X ⟶ Y) (f' : X' ⟶ Y') (hf : Flat f.left) (hlfp : LocallyOfFinitePresentation f.left) (hf' : Flat f'.left) (hlfp' : LocallyOfFinitePresentation f'.left) (a : X' ≅ X) (b : Y' ≅ Y), a.hom ≫ f = f' ≫ b.hom → D f' hf' hlfp' = a.hom.left ⁻¹ᵁ (D f hf hlfp)) (hbase : ∀ {X Y X' Y' : Over S} (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y' ⟶ Y) (f' : X' ⟶ Y') (p : X' ⟶ X) (hf : Flat f.left) (hlfp : LocallyOfFinitePresentation f.left) (hg : Flat g.left) (hglfp : LocallyOfFinitePresentation g.left) (hf' : Flat f'.left) (hlfp' : LocallyOfFinitePresentation f'.left), IsPullback p.left f'.left f.left g.left → D f' hf' hlfp' = p.left ⁻¹ᵁ (D f hf hlfp)) {V R : Over S} (s t : R ⟶ V) (hinj : ∀ T : Over S, Function.Injective (fun r : T ⟶ R ↦ (r ≫ s, r ≫ t))) (hrel : ∀ T : Over S, Equivalence (fun a b : T ⟶ V ↦ ∃ r : T ⟶ R, r ≫ s = a ∧ r ≫ t = b)) [hs : Flat s.left] [ht : Flat t.left] [hslfp : LocallyOfFinitePresentation s.left] [htlfp : LocallyOfFinitePresentation t.left] (e : V ⟶ R) (hes : e ≫ s = 𝟙 V) (het : e ≫ t = 𝟙 V) : D s hs hslfp = t.left ⁻¹ᵁ (e.left ⁻¹ᵁ (D s hs hslfp))

reviewed_lean.note: Lean relation_open_locus_descent matches node and Stacks 04LH (g=id, flat+lfp). D is defined only on flat+lfp morphisms over S. hiso has the correct direction and is implied by hbase. hbase covers any pullback square with f,g,f' flat+lfp and no condition on p. hinj/hrel use the same equivalence-relation encoding as the consumer exists_flat_relation_cm_open. The four instances on s,t; e is supplied with s e=t e=id, which adds no hypothesis since reflexivity gives it and injectivity makes it unique. The conclusion D s = t^{-1}(e^{-1}(D s)) is the node's D_s=t^{-1}(W). Edge cases (empty, diagonal, indiscrete, constant assignments) are fine. The node changed only in lean, and its statement matches the file verbatim. stmt_deps are all existing Mathlib records; no name clash; sorry only; docstrings carry the source, blueprint id and the four steps. Advisory: private proof-only imports are unused by the statement.
